---
title: "Demultiplexing"
---

## Overview

After sequencing, reads must be demultiplexed (assigned to wells) and analyzed to identify the variant in each well.

## Pipeline Overview

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Raw FASTQ] --> B[Outer Demux<br/>Plate indices]
    B --> C[Inner Demux<br/>Well barcodes]
    C --> D[Alignment<br/>to Reference]
    D --> E[Variant<br/>Calling]
    E --> F[Well<br/>Assignments]
```

## Using the CLI

### Basic Usage

```bash
usortm demux project/ --fastq data.fastq
```

This runs the full pipeline and saves results to `project/demux_output/`.

### With Custom Barcodes

```bash
usortm demux project/ \
    --fastq data.fastq \
    --barcodes my_barcodes.csv \
    --reference reference.fasta
```

### Output Files

```
project/demux_output/
├── demux_summary.json     # Statistics
└── well_assignments.csv   # Variant per well
```

**well_assignments.csv format:**

```csv
plate,well,reads,variant,consensus_fraction
1,A1,523,K44A,0.97
1,A2,412,G45A,0.95
1,A3,89,low_coverage,0.00
```

## Manual Demultiplexing

For custom pipelines, here's the general approach:

### 1. Outer (Plate) Demultiplexing

Using Dorado for ONT data:

```bash
dorado demux data.fastq \
    --kit-name nextera_bcs_trim \
    --barcode-arrangement nextera_bcs_trim.toml \
    --barcode-sequences nextera_i7rc.fasta \
    --barcode-both-ends \
    --no-trim \
    -o NXT_demux/
```

### 2. Inner (Well) Demultiplexing

```bash
for plate in $(seq 1 8); do
    dorado demux NXT_demux/barcode${plate}.bam \
        --kit-name evseq_bcs \
        --barcode-arrangement evSeq_bcs.toml \
        --barcode-sequences evSeq_DI${plate}.fasta \
        --barcode-both-ends \
        --no-trim \
        --emit-fastq \
        -o evSeq_demux/plate${plate}/
done
```

### 3. Alignment

Using minimap2:

```bash
minimap2 -ax map-ont reference.fasta well_reads.fastq > aligned.sam
```

### 4. Variant Calling

Extract consensus sequence and compare to reference:

```python
# Pseudocode
for well in wells:
    reads = get_reads(well)
    if len(reads) < min_reads:
        continue
    consensus = build_consensus(reads)
    variant = call_variant(consensus, reference)
    record(well, variant)
```

## Configuration Files

### nextera_bcs_trim.toml

```toml
[arrangement]
name = "nextera_bcs_trim"
kit = "CZI"
mask1_front = "AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACAC"
mask1_rear = "TCGTCGGCAGCGTC"
mask2_front = "CAAGCAGAAGACGGCATACGAGAT"
mask2_rear = "GTCTCGTGGGCTCGG"
barcode1_pattern = "CZB-NXT-i5-%02i"
barcode2_pattern = "CZB-NXT-i7-%02i"
first_index = 1
last_index = 8

[scoring]
max_barcode_penalty = 6
min_barcode_penalty_dist = 2
min_separation_only_dist = 5
min_flank_score = 0.8
```

### evSeq_bcs.toml

```toml
[arrangement]
name = "evseq_bcs"
kit = "evSeq"
mask1_front = "TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG"
mask1_rear = "CACCCAAGACCACTCTCCGG"
mask2_front = "GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG"
mask2_rear = "CGGTGTGCGAAGTAGGTGC"
barcode1_pattern = "evSeq-FBC-%02i"
barcode2_pattern = "evSeq-RBC-%02i"
first_index = 1
last_index = 96

[scoring]
max_barcode_penalty = 2
min_barcode_penalty_dist = 1
min_separation_only_dist = 3
min_flank_score = 0.7
```

## Quality Metrics

### Read Assignment Rate

Typical: 60-70% of reads assigned to wells

Low assignment (<50%) may indicate:

- Barcode synthesis errors
- Sequencing quality issues
- Incorrect barcode configuration

### Wells with Sufficient Reads

Target: >85% of wells with growth have >100 reads

Low coverage may indicate:

- Insufficient sequencing depth
- PCR bias
- Sample loss during pooling

### Consensus Quality

Wells should have >80% of reads supporting the consensus sequence.

Low consensus fraction may indicate:

- Mixed cultures (doublets)
- PCR chimeras
- Sequencing errors

## Troubleshooting

### Many Unassigned Reads

1. Check barcode sequences match your primers
2. Verify TOML configuration
3. Relax scoring parameters if needed

### Missing Wells

1. Verify growth in those wells (OD check)
2. Check for PCR failures
3. Confirm barcode primer distribution

### Mixed Variants in Single Well

1. Likely a doublet sort
2. Check sort parameters
3. Can sometimes resolve with stricter consensus calling
